CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in fingers and pain in right wrist.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a landscaper presenting with right wrist pain and numbness that has been ongoing for several months. Symptoms began insidiously without clear precipitating event. Patient notes symptoms are most prominent at night, often waking with hand asleep requiring shaking out. Numbness appears to affect all fingers but is more pronounced in thumb and pointer finger, with occasional numbness in fifth finger as well. Patient denies similar symptoms in right hand. Patient attributes repetitive heavy labor in landscaping work (raking, digging) as potential contributing factor. Denies dropping objects, though reports difficulty with grip strength and sensation in left hand.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports numbness and tingling in left hand fingers, particularly thumb and pointer finger. Denies problems with right hand. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in landscaping performing heavy labor with repetitive motions including raking and digging. Consumes alcohol occasionally, typically one to two beers on Friday and Saturday evenings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs auscultated and noted to be good. Grip strength decreased on left hand compared to right. Sensory examination of right hand intact to touch on all fingers, though sensation feels slightly different on thumb compared to pointer finger. Bilateral positive Tinel's sign elicited upon percussion of wrists.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. Plan includes: (1) Activity modification with delegation of repetitive motions to employees for several weeks; (2) Wrist splint; (3) Ibuprofen 600 mg every six hours; (4) EMG study to measure electrical impulses in fingers; (5) Follow-up office visit in two weeks to assess response to conservative treatment and determine need for further diagnostic testing or possible surgical intervention for nerve decompression.
